title: Windows and Doors Rebates in Kingston 2026: Renters, Owners and the $100 Rebate
desc: Kingston window and door rebates for 2026: $100 per rough opening under Home Renovation Savings, in a city where 44% of households rent.
h1: Windows and Doors Rebates in Kingston
lead: Kingston has 57,835 households, and 44% rent. Only owners can claim the window and door rebate, and only in the right kind of building.
cards_heading: What the Home Renovation Savings program pays for windows and doors in Kingston
cards_intro: We re-read the program's page and its eligibility requirements on October 3, 2026. Windows and doors are paid only inside the assessment stream, so every amount here comes with an assessment and at least two upgrades.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: One payment per opening in an outside wall, not per unit. A bay window with three panes in one opening earns $100.

cards.title: Smallest qualifying job
cards.note: Three window openings, or one door, sliding door or skylight opening, count as one qualified measure. Two windows alone earn nothing.

cards.title: Home energy assessment
cards.note: $600 comes back when the program is completed. Covers the cost of the first and the follow-up assessment once the program is completed.

cards.title: Three or more upgrades
cards.note: Windows count as one upgrade. Insulation, air sealing and a heat pump water heater are the others in this stream.

cards.title: Program cap
cards.note: $10,000 for homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood, and $5,000 for homes heated by Enbridge gas.

after_cards: The program is run by Enbridge Gas and Save on Energy. Post-audits must be scheduled by November 30, 2026 and completed by December 31, 2026, or within 180 days of your first assessment, whichever comes first.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 57,835 households in Kingston, with 56% owning and 44% renting. Only 63% live in an eligible house type. 17% live in apartment buildings of five or more storeys and 16% in smaller buildings, and 2,190 households live in duplexes. Many Kingston buildings are therefore outside the program. If you rent, the landlord owns the openings and must apply.

53% of Kingston households live in homes built before 1981, and 12,990 are owner-occupied detached houses from that period. Major repairs were reported by 6.5%. An older house with heritage features may have windows that are worth restoring rather than replacing, and restoration does not qualify for the rebate. The program pays only for complete ENERGY STAR certified replacement units.
Landlords who live in the building

An owner who lives in a house with a rented room can apply if the house was built as a single dwelling and has a central heating system. A building that was built as multiple units, including duplexes and triplexes, is not eligible even when the owner lives there.

The January average low is -9.0°C and the 2015 to 2024 record was -29.2°C. Utilities Kingston is the electric utility, but it does not change the window rebate. Heating fuel does matter for the cap: $10,000 for electricity, oil, propane or wood and $5,000 for Enbridge gas.
What the audits cost and return

The program pays $600 back to offset the cost of the initial and the follow-up assessments, once the program is complete. The audit price is set by the service organization, so ask what it charges before you book. For an owner with a smaller project, such as three window openings, the audit cost and the paperwork can be a large share of the benefit, so consider whether a larger bundle makes more sense.
claim_steps: Confirm you own the home, it has been occupied for six months and it is one of the eligible house types.
Book the first home energy assessment with a registered energy advisor before any work starts.
Choose at least one more upgrade to pair with the windows, and get quotes that count rough openings the way the program does.
Check whether the building was built as a single dwelling.
Have a professional install complete windows or doors with frames, keep the ENERGY STAR labels on until the follow-up assessment, and book it.
faq: Can Kingston renters claim the window rebate?
No. Only complete ENERGY STAR certified replacement units qualify.
No, even if the owner lives in one unit.
